statement: Combined FY2027 capex of the 5 largest AI/cloud spenders >= 1.2x FY2026 (Securities filings; on FY2027 filings)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable in 2023. Context: during 2023 some of the largest spenders cut capex year on year (one paused data-centre construction to switch to an AI-oriented design) while others raised AI-driven spending; by Q3 2023 calls, the large spenders guided to higher capex in 2024, citing AI compute. Full-year 2023 aggregates were only published in Feb 2024 and are excluded under the as-of rule.

items.summary: A top cloud/AI spender reported Q3 2023 capex of $8 bn, 'reflecting a meaningful increase in our investments in AI compute', and said 2024 aggregate capex would exceed full-year 2023.
items.detail: Alphabet, 2023 Q3 earnings call transcript, 2023-10-24 (verified via web_extract this run).

items.summary: Another top spender's Q3 2023 capex fell to $6.8 bn from $9.52 bn a year earlier during a data-centre construction pause for an AI-oriented redesign; it guided full-year 2023 capex to $27-29 bn and 2024 to $30-35 bn, with AI the largest area of increased investment.
items.detail: DatacenterDynamics, 'Meta's CapEx drops almost $3bn during data center construction pause', 2023-10-26 (verified via web_extract this run), reporting Meta's Q3 2023 results and CFO remarks.

items.summary: A third top spender reported quarterly results framed around 'infusing AI across every layer of our tech stack', with cloud revenue up 24% year on year; the release itself gives no capex figure.
items.detail: Microsoft FY24 Q1 earnings press release, 2023-10-24 (verified via web_extract this run; capex not in the extracted release text, so no value recorded).
